source.title: MSRS: Training Multimodal Speech Recognition Models from Scratch with Sparse Mask Optimization
source.authors: Adriana Fernandez-Lopez; Hong-Lie Chen; Ping-Chuan Ma; Lu Yin; Qiao Xiao; Stavros Petridis; Shi-Wei Liu; Maja Pantic

record.tranche_reason: The study reports from-scratch training outcomes for VSR and AVSR speech models, a new modality and task setting relative to the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-set WER and describes convergence, but does not report training classification error. Its speech-recognition results therefore do not measure the specific CIFAR classification-error behavior or the initialization, depth, learning-rate, and normalization comparisons named in V1–V6. Table 4 comparisons are included where they report outcomes of training from random initialization.
record.test_reason: The study measures speech-recognition test WER and convergence under sparse-mask regularization. It does not measure near-zero CIFAR training error, teacher-student spurious minima, depth degradation with versus without identity shortcuts, activation-matched initialization, stability-threshold dynamics, or batch-normalization benefits. Its own results therefore test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate when restricted to the tested sparse methods and architectures. The authors conclude that MSRS learns sparse masks early, improves gradient flow, and enables from-scratch VSR/AVSR training, with subsequent dense or sparse training. They attribute this to masking weights affected by vanishing gradients; the experiments support improved convergence but do not independently establish that causal explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses AdamW and proposes MSRS mask optimization for speech recognition; the claim versions concern SGD or Adam classification-error outcomes and other specified interventions. The reported outcomes are test WER, not training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that MSRS success depends strongly on λ; they also report that pruning slows as dataset size falls, and that the λ value may need adjustment below 300 hours.

fits_no_version.finding: Dense randomly initialized VSR models fail to converge, while LayerScale and MSRS enable useful test WER. Sparse MSRS models also train with reduced data; AVSR models achieve competitive noisy-speech results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-mask optimization can enable from-scratch training of the tested VSR and AVSR architectures, with performance depending on data quantity, sparsity, and training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying masks learned by MSRS to dense-model gradients improves convergence and produces 52.1% test WER.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient masks learned through MSRS can improve optimization of the tested small VSR model.

record.problems: The reported metric is test WER rather than training classification error. No uncertainty estimates are stated in the reported tables. The AVSR section describes staged training that transitions from MSRS training on a subset of data to dense training on the entire dataset.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 has multiple pretrained and comparator entries; they were left out because the extraction focuses on the study's random-initialization training outcomes. Table 3's remaining SNR-specific WER values for the same AVSR models were left out to keep the record focused; all are reported in Table 3.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
All parts: controlled depth degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal propagation across depth, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and trainable depth.
All parts: learning rates relative to a measured stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
All parts: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. Generic references to vanishing gradients, initialization, width, depth, and Fixup do not make these experiments tests of the specified versions. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6; the reported WER outcomes themselves remain readable.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, including corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus identity-shortcut depth comparisons, and the named special-initialization and normalization-free methods.
Comparisons of activation-matched, Gaussian, and orthogonal initializations and their effects on depth and training speed.
Training behavior above a stability limit and sharpness behavior during full-batch training.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.
